angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 709,614 km at 123.14 pc = 0.08 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 8.1211 +/- 0.0113 mas (same row, RUWE 0.85): 123.14 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.02 +/- 0.09 solar radii from Marcy et al. 2014, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of Kepler-96 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014ApJS..210...20M/abstract): 709,614 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1 +/- 0.06 solar masses from Marcy et al. 2014, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of Kepler-96 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014ApJS..210...20M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5690 +/- 73 K from Marcy et al. 2014, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-96 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014ApJS..210...20M/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Marcy et al. 2014, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-96 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014ApJS..210...20M/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/kepler-96.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.421, rounded to two decimals
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of Kepler-96 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.04 dex, from Marcy et al. 2014 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014ApJS..210...20M/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of Kepler-96 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.05231, from Gajdoš et al. 2019 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019RAA....19...41G/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of Kepler-96 (pscomppars): age 2.34 Gyr, from Marcy et al. 2014 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014ApJS..210...20M/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of Kepler-96 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 0.5 km/s, from Marcy et al. 2014 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014ApJS..210...20M/abstract)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
